component.name: YazSes
component.summary: Offline voice dictation that types into the focused app

description.p: YazSes is offline voice dictation. Hold a key, speak, release — your words are transcribed on your own CPU and typed into whatever window has focus: editor, browser, terminal or chat.
After installation and a one-time model download, speech recognition runs locally. Audio and transcripts are not sent to any cloud service, and there is no account, API key, GPU or subscription.

ul.li: Transcribe an audio or video file to text, SRT, WebVTT, Markdown or JSON
Label who said what, using speaker models that run on your machine
Capture a whole meeting hands-free and get a speaker-labelled transcript
Optionally write minutes with a local language model you supply

description.p: Known limitations, so they are not a surprise after installing:

ul.li: The first run downloads a speech model (a few hundred megabytes) and needs a network connection. Transcription itself works with networking disabled.
The shipped models are tuned for English. Other languages need a multilingual model selected explicitly, and accuracy varies.
Hold-to-talk needs permission to read keyboard events. If your system declines that permission, the daemon starts and looks healthy but never hears the key.
Typing into other applications depends on the sandbox permissions granted to this build. Where injection is not permitted, dictated text is placed on the clipboard instead, and you paste it yourself.
Desktop only — there is no mobile version.
